title: This Bird Builds an Optical Illusion to Win a Mate

scenes.text: This bird builds an optical illusion to win a mate.
The great bowerbird lays out stones, shells and bones in a courtyard.
But he sorts them by size. Small near the female, large farther away.
From her spot, the court looks smaller and his decorations look bigger.
Scientists swapped the order. Within three days, he put it all back.
The better the illusion, the more mates he wins.

description:
This bird builds an optical illusion to win a mate.
Great bowerbirds arrange objects by size so the court looks different from the female's viewpoint. The best illusions went to the males with the most mates.
How did he learn that trick? Tell us below.
thumbnail_text: BIRD BUILDS AN ILLUSION TO WIN
first_comment: Scientists still don't know whether the bowerbird uses real perspective, trial and error, or a rule of thumb. Which would you bet on?
